prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1275; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver following a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed the center line while turning. Insured states she felt neck stiffness shortly after the impact and was evaluated at an urgent care clinic the same day. Vehicle is drivable but front bumper and hood damage noted in photos submitted. Police report number provided and pending retrieval.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant, who is not represented by counsel. Claimant confirmed ongoing neck pain and lower back soreness, rated as moderate and worse in the mornings. Claimant has been prescribed muscle relaxants and a course of physical therapy. Explained the claims process, the medical documentation needed, and that she may choose to consult an attorney at any time. Requested copies of all treatment records and bills.

Entry 3: Reviewed the independent appraisal on the claimant's vehicle. Damage is consistent with the reported impact speed and direction, with no airbag deployment. Repair estimate is within the expected range for this model. Requested a supplemental photo set of the rear seat and passenger areas to rule out secondary contact.

Entry 4: Received the urgent care records and first physical therapy evaluation. Diagnosis is cervical and lumbar strain with no fractures or imaging abnormalities. Records note reduced range of motion in the neck and a plan of six weeks of therapy. Medical review scheduled to confirm treatment is reasonable and related to the collision.

Entry 5: Left a voicemail for the claimant to confirm her current symptoms and therapy attendance. Claimant returned the call and reported improvement in lower back symptoms but persistent neck stiffness. Advised her of the next steps, including the rental reimbursement limits on her policy and the timeline for the injury evaluation. Diary set for follow-up in two weeks.
